invocations.content:
**No.** The page doesn't show `httpx.Client` accepting a `retries` keyword. It only documents `retries` on `HTTPTransport`, which you pass to the client through the `transport` argument. The page says: "HTTPX's `Client` also accepts a `transport` argument." The documented pattern is:

`transport = httpx.HTTPTransport(retries=1)`
`client = httpx.Client(transport=transport)`

**Scope:** Retries apply only to connection failures. The page says requests are retried when "an `httpx.ConnectError` or an `httpx.ConnectTimeout` occurs." Because only these two exceptions are listed, retries don't appear to cover read timeouts or other errors.

For other retry behavior, the page says that if you need "other forms of retry behaviors," you should consider general-purpose tools. It names tenacity as an example and mentions read/write errors and 503 responses as cases it doesn't cover.

Web search results for query: "httpx Client retries argument TypeError HTTPTransport retries connection errors"

Links: [{"title":"pypi.org","url":"https://pypi.org/project/rhttpx/"},{"title":"ai.pydantic.dev","url":"https://ai.pydantic.dev/api/retries"},{"title":"glama.ai","url":"https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/@pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/9aa6dd40efafd93c04c19c2ef5596a454906ca53/pydantic_ai_slim/pydantic_ai/retries.py"},{"title":"retries of AsyncHTTPTransport and HTTPTransport is not passes to pools with proxy but only ordinary pool","url":"https://github.com/encode/httpx/discussions/2988"},{"title":"httpx-retries 0.4.6","url":"https://simple-repository.app.cern.ch/project/httpx_retries"},{"title":"github.com","url":"https://github.com/encode/httpx/pull/784"},{"title":"> ## Documentation Index","url":"https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/models/http-request-retries/index.md"},{"title":"pydantic.dev","url":"https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/advanced-features/retries/"},{"title":"http request retries","url":"https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/models/http-request-retries/"}]

The search didn't turn up a page that explains this exact TypeError, but the results point to the likely cause and fix.

**Likely cause:** `httpx.Client` has no `retries` keyword argument. Retry support lives on the transport layer, so `httpx.Client(retries=...)` fails with a TypeError. A third-party package, rhttpx, describes the same kind of error: it raises a TypeError if unsupported keyword arguments are supplied to the underlying httpx.AsyncClient constructor.

**Fix:** Put the retry setting on the transport instead. Per a GitHub discussion, AsyncConnectionPool has the argument of retries passed in, and the same setting exists on the sync transport. A typical pattern is:

```python
import httpx

transport = httpx.HTTPTransport(retries=3)
with httpx.Client(transport=transport) as client:
    r = client.get("https://example.com")
```

**Caveats:**
- From my own knowledge (not confirmed by these results), `HTTPTransport(retries=...)` only retries connection-establishment failures, not read or write errors or 5xx responses.
- The same GitHub discussion reports that the retries setting is not passed to pools with proxy but only ordinary pool, so it may not apply when you use proxies.
- An older proposal for a `httpx.Retries` object (PR #784) appears in the results, but I couldn't confirm it was merged, so don't rely on it without checking your installed httpx version.

**If you need status-code or read-error retries:** Use a dedicated package. The httpx-retries package offers a RetryTransport that you add to the client, and it accepts a urllib3-style Retry configuration. Alternatively, pydantic-ai provides tenacity-based transports, and its docs note that without a response validator, only network errors and timeouts will result in a retry.

resulting_evidence:
**Recommendation: use the transport-level retry that HTTPX documents. Don't pass `retries=` to `httpx.Client`.**

**Explanation of the error.** The log records `httpx.Client(retries=3)` raising `TypeError`. `Client` has no `retries` keyword. Retry configuration is a property of the transport, and `Client` accepts a `transport` argument.

**Documented supported alternative.** The [HTTPX transports docs](https://www.python-httpx.org/advanced/transports/) show:

```python
transport = httpx.HTTPTransport(retries=3)
client = httpx.Client(transport=transport)
```

Per the same page, retries apply only to `httpx.ConnectError` and `httpx.ConnectTimeout`. They do not cover read timeouts, write errors, or 5xx responses. This fits the project note that calls need "connection-error retries," so this is a direct match.

**Limits of this research:**
- I read the current HTTPX docs, not the 0.28.1 docs specifically. Confirm the `retries` parameter on `HTTPTransport` against the pinned `httpx==0.28.1` (e.g., `python -c "import httpx, inspect; print(inspect.signature(httpx.HTTPTransport))"`).
- A [GitHub discussion](https://github.com/encode/httpx/discussions/2988) appeared in search results, and it reports that transport retries may not apply to proxy pools. I only saw its title, not its content, so treat that as an unverified lead. Check it if you use proxies.
- An older `httpx.Retries` proposal ([PR #784](https://github.com/encode/httpx/pull/784)) appeared in results. I could not confirm it was merged, so don't rely on it.
- For status-code or read-error retries, the docs point to general tools such as tenacity. A third-party `httpx-retries` package also exists, but I did not evaluate it.
